newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch probe British child porn murder allegations.
newsitem.headline: Dutch probe British child porn murder allegations.

text.p: Dutch police confirmed on Monday they were probing allegations of a series of child "snuff movie" murders by a British paedophile ring in Hoofddorp near Amsterdam in the early 1990s.

"After consultations with the Justice Ministry, we have mounted a preliminary inquiry based on information supplied to us by the producer of a British television documentary," police spokesman Alfred Ellwanger said.

He said the producer had passed on information gathered in making the film "The Boy Business", which alleges that a British-led paedophile ring operating in Amsterdam and nearby Hoofddorp abducted and murdered homeless teenage boys from Britain and eastern Europe.

According to the programme, due to be screened on Britain's independent ITV channel on Tuesday, the ring made and distributed at least five so-called "snuff-porn videos" in which teenage and pre-teen boys were sexually abused to death.
The children's dead bodies were later dumped on the outskirts of Amsterdam, the documentary claims.
The allegations were also detailed in Saturday's edition of the British newspaper The Guardian, which said it had carried its own two-year investigation into the matter.

The paper detailed one video known as the "Bjorn Tape", allegedly made in Amsterdam in 1990, which begins with a man entering a room carrying the limp figure of a young boy, his hands tied and his head covered with a hood.

The film has been distributed to paedophiles all over Europe and stills from it released to the documentary makers by British police's specialist Paedophilia Unit at Scotland Yard in London, the paper said.
Ellwanger said Hoofddorp police were checking the allegations after information was passed on by the documentary's makers.
"Based on the outcome of this preliminary inquiry, police will decide whether to launch a criminal investigation," he said.

Amsterdam police said that their specialist child pornography investigation team had previously investigated similar allegations in 1990 and 1993, but that these inquiries had yielded no concrete results.
"This particular story has been running for a number of years, and our child pornography investigation team has repeatedly looked into it," police spokesman Cees Rameau said.
He said Amsterdam's most recent investigations into the affair had been based on material handed over by the documentary makers three weeks ago.
"Based on their information we saw no reason to reopen the case, although of course we are monitoring the situation and will watch tomorrow's documentary with great interest," he said.
